title: I Wanted to See the World

pages.title: The Cost of Going
captions: A year at Paris 1 would mean graduating a year later. I thought about that choice for a long time.
alt: A young man stands in a quiet university room; below, his hand pauses beside plain travel papers.

pages.title: The World Beside Dad
captions: I grew up in a coastal village in Xianxiang, Ningbo. My earliest journeys were in my father’s delivery truck.
I often stayed in the truck with him. At New Year, visits to relatives and days out with my sister brought city life a little closer.
In fourth grade, I won the district high jump competition. Running and basketball were also part of my school years.
alt: A delivery truck follows the Ningbo coast; a child rides beside his father; the same boy clears a high-jump bar.

pages.title: Almost Through
captions: I qualified for a top high school’s special admissions exam, then missed the minimum score. That setback stayed with me.
I returned to preparing, finished first in my class and entered Zhengshi High School. I still felt the distance from what I had hoped for.
My university entrance exam also fell short of my hopes. I chose Zhejiang Gongshang University over a Project 211 university outside Zhejiang.
alt: A hand holds a plain result sheet; a small student stands in a school corridor; an older student crosses a university courtyard.

pages.title: Someone Beside Me
captions: As my underbite became severe, nicknames and mockery made me afraid of other people’s gaze. Some nights, I hid in the dormitory bathroom and cried.
My family came with me to Shanghai Ninth People’s Hospital. I decided to have corrective jaw surgery.
First came orthodontics. It lasted more than two years—much longer than I had expected.
alt: A young man’s pronounced pre-surgery underbite is shown respectfully in profile; a quiet bathroom doorway, family in a waiting room and appointment papers mark a long wait.

pages.title: A Voice of My Own
captions: At university, I studied French. There was another thread running through those years: teaching English.
I had started teaching after high school. I kept teaching through study, treatment and everything that followed.
In my junior year’s second semester, I finally had surgery. Afterward, I began to regain confidence in everyday life.
I had consistently ranked first in my major. Two months after surgery, I secured postgraduate admission to SWUFE and received the National Scholarship.
alt: French study and standing English teaching coexist with treatment; quiet recovery and an open campus scene follow, without a surgical procedure or invented award ceremony.

pages.title: This Time, I Chose
captions: Back at that choice, I finally decided to go to Paris.
Before leaving, four months supporting overseas talent sourcing for ByteDance’s Seed team brought me closer to AI.
I left with a new direction taking shape.
alt: Hands prepare a travel bag; a wide rear view shows recruitment support without identifiable candidate data; a small traveller walks through an airport passage.

pages.title: A World I Could Speak To
captions: During my year at Paris 1, I also spent a year learning Spanish.
The limits of my language are the limits of my world. The child who wanted to see beyond the truck window had finally made it here.
alt: A Spanish-learning scene in Paris, an unhurried city street and a full-length walk beside the Seine give the story room to breathe.

pages.title: More World Beyond the Window
captions: After Paris, I joined Tencent Cloud as a direct-sales intern. I kept learning cloud computing and building with AI.
I am still teaching English. That thread has continued since I left high school.
Going out into the world has given me more worlds to explore.
alt: A wide professional conversation, engaged English teaching and an open coastal view echo the childhood window without a final triumph pose.
